text.p: The following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian President Milan Kucan met Hungarian President Arpad Goencz during his short vacations in Slovenia.
- Heavy rain with hail flooded some streets of Slovenia's capital Ljubljana.

- The number of visitors to the Slovenian coastal resorts reached this season's record high with 15,305 visitors this weekend. This was a five percent increase compared to last year. Visits by foreign tourists was up 31 percent, while domestic visits fell by 12 percent.
- The average duration of sick leave of Slovenian workers in 1996 was 20 days and remained within the European average, the national health insurance company said.
- The capacity utilisation of Slovenia's only nuclear power plant Krsko in July reached 98.9 percent. The power plant produced 456.4 million kiloWatt hours of electricity.

- Slovenian runner Brigita Bukovec won the fourth place in the 100 metre hurdle race in the athletics World Championships in Athens on Sunday. This was Slovenia's biggest success so far in athletic world championships.
- Slovenian rower Luka Spik won gold in the European Championship for Juniors in the Belgian town Hazenwinkel.
- A Slovenian truck driver was arrested in London on Friday following an attempt to smuggle 200 kilos of heroine, worth about $160 million.
